structured_output.summary: Phase 8 (Qualification and delivery) is substantively complete and the evidence survives inspection rather than resting on prose. The recorded gate (docs/checks/phase-08.json, SHA 5e11f6ae…) contains all 74 commands that tools/check_phase.py:138-163 defines for phase 8, every one with exit_code 0, bound to source 48fa78ae… with source_unchanged true; I independently recounted the command set (48 inherited + 26 new = 74) and found no non-zero exit code anywhere in the report. The underlying checks are real work, not stubs: scripts/check-dependencies.py performs a fresh authoritative RustSec clone/fetch with pinned cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 (0 vulnerabilities, empty warnings, 206 packages, freshHead true); scripts/check-package.py extracts the actual .crate with a hardened reader and runs 145 minimal + 201 all-feature packaged unit tests, examples, a doctest and an external 3,820-probe consumer against the extracted archive, which closes the Phase-4 packaged-unit-tests follow-up through the 18-specimen src/fixtures/model-regressions.json corpus derived from independently executed frozen Zod; contracts/qualification.json projects all 448 frozen operations with implemented/contract-verified/option-parity complete, liveVerified 17, unexplainedGaps 0, and tools/qualification.py refuses family-wide or constructor promotion; the live receipt (docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-05.json) is sanitized, bounded (24 service requests + 1 token exchange, 15s/op, 0 retries), records 3x403 and 2x400 honestly, and binds to a runtime fingerprint over src/ and examples/. Platform, CI, release, stability, changelog and README documentation consistently separate implementation parity from offline contracts, live acceptance, platform execution and publication, and the outstanding delivery acts (clean-commit archive proof, push to origin) are explicitly scheduled rather than claimed. Security posture is good: credential-free verification, env scrubbing of PANW_/AIRS_/SCM_ in every runner, 0600 private outputs, no secrets in any committed check artifact (grep for secret-shaped patterns across docs/checks finds nothing), forbid(unsafe_code), and the new json_decode.rs boundary is a bounded non-recursive guard with no bypass at the SSE truthiness path. The deductions are: two orphan evidence files in docs/checks/ with no committed generator and no gate binding (one of them not referenced by any doc at all), a live-failure taxonomy that cannot distinguish a native request-shape defect from a genuine service-side rejection for the two 400s, a receipt annotation rule that lets an early success mask a later failure of the same method, and near-absent rustdoc item documentation/doctests for a public crate at its final documentation phase.

findings.description: This 100-process stress report is cited as qualification evidence for the tracing-capture-registration-isolation candidate in docs/phase-status.json:515, but no generator exists in the repository (grep for "tracing-stress" matches only docs/phase-status.json), it is not part of commands_for(8) in tools/check_phase.py:138-163, and no tool verifies or re-binds it. Unlike every other file in docs/checks/, it cannot be reproduced or detected as stale, so it is an unverifiable artifact sitting among gate-produced ones. The deterministic regression itself (observability::tests::subscriberless_first_callsite_registration_keeps_local_capture_enabled) does run in the gate, which limits the impact.
findings.required_fix: Commit the stress runner (for example scripts/check-tracing-stress.py) and either add it to the phase gate or reference it from docs/OBSERVABILITY.md with its exact reproduction command; otherwise relabel the file in docs/phase-status.json and docs/OBSERVABILITY.md as a one-off unreproducible observation rather than qualification evidence.

findings.description: A credential-leak scan receipt (627 git-visible files checked, 0 selected client identity/secret matches) sits in the evidence directory with no committed generator and no citation anywhere in the repository: grep for "private-material" and "gitVisibleFilesChecked" matches only the file itself. It is not listed in docs/phase-status.json scope_evidence, not referenced by docs/SECURITY.md, and not executed by the gate, so the one piece of evidence that the AGENTS.md credential-exclusion rule was actually checked is itself unverifiable and unmaintained.
findings.required_fix: Commit the scanner that produced this receipt, invoke it from the phase gate or document its exact command, and cite the receipt from docs/SECURITY.md and docs/phase-status.json; if it is not intended as standing evidence, delete it from docs/checks/.

findings.description: failure_class maps every 400/405/409/422 to "service_contract_rejection", and the receipt row schema in tools/live_evidence.py:129 permits only operation/classification/status/errorKind/remoteOutcome/workflowAccepted. The two recorded 400s (iam.scopes.create and gateway.workspaces.provision, docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-05.json:212-234) are therefore recorded, and explained in tools/qualification.py:27 as "The service rejected the submitted controlled contract", in a way that is indistinguishable from a native request-shape defect. docs/implementation-plan.md:121 requires provider incompatibility, backend failures and missing SDK implementation to remain distinct classifications; here an SDK body/field error in the two headline mutation workflows (including the sole Phase-7 provisioning workflow) would be auto-attributed to the service. docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:12-16 hedges that no vendor specification establishes a cause, but does not state that a native defect is unexcluded.
findings.required_fix: Record the already-allowlisted ProblemDetails code and field-error names for rejection classes in the receipt row (extending the require_keys allowlist in tools/live_evidence.py), and state explicitly in docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md that the cause of the two 400s is unestablished and a native request-shape defect is not excluded.

findings.description: In load(), once a baseline method has been annotated "verified", any later probe for the same baseline id is skipped ("if previous and previous['liveAcceptance'] == 'verified': continue"). A method that succeeds in the probe phase and then fails during cleanup or reconciliation (for example iam.scopes.get or iam.scopes.delete appearing in both report["probes"] and report["cleanup"]) retains a verified live classification in contracts/qualification.json, hiding the later failure from the matrix.
findings.required_fix: Record every observation for a baseline id (or select the worst outcome) and require an explicit reviewed reconciliation when a method has both a success and a later failure in the same receipt.

findings.description: Rustdoc item coverage is partial and unenforced at the phase whose criteria include final documentation and API examples. Cargo.toml:12-16 (workspace lints) enables only unsafe_code=forbid and clippy::all, with no missing_docs lint, and the packaged doctest run contains exactly one test (docs/checks/phase-08-package-1.99.0.json:769, the examples/foundation.rs block embedded at crates/scm-sdk/src/lib.rs:6). Public entry points such as Scanner::new (line 47), for_region (51), client (62), sync_scan (65) and query_by_report_ids (161) carry no item documentation, so generated rustdoc for a 448-method public API will show many undocumented items even though docs/*.md guides are thorough.
findings.required_fix: Enable #![warn(missing_docs)] (or document the deliberate exception in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md with the chosen coverage boundary) and add at least a one-line doc comment plus a short no_run example to each product client entry point.

limitations: Read-only review: I could not execute any command, so I verified the recorded stdout, exit codes, hashes and artifact contents rather than re-running the 74 gate commands, the dependency audit, the package extraction or the Rust test suites.

I could not diff the working tree against HEAD (phase 8 work is uncommitted across ~50 modified and several untracked files), so my assessment of changed source is based on reading current file contents, not on the delta reviewed in earlier phases.

I did not verify the SHA-256 of the reviewed source or of docs/checks/phase-08.json myself; I accepted the values stated in the prompt and cross-checked them against docs/phase-status.json and the check report fields.

I spot-checked the 1,774-line phase-08.json and the 448-row qualification matrix rather than reading every row; I confirmed absence of non-zero exit codes by pattern search and read the head, the phase-8-specific middle section and the tail.

I did not read .local/typescript or any credential/tenant file, so frozen-baseline parity claims (2,630 exports, 448 methods, 3,820 capabilities) rest on the recorded extractor/oracle outputs and the tooling's self-tests, not on independent inspection of the TypeScript source.

Child evidence files (per-feature rust reports, cross reports, package reports) are not hash-bound into phase-08.json, so I verified their summary lines as echoed in the gate stdout and read two of them in full rather than all 51.
